disposition: retain as an unpromoted candidate; remediate and split the Web UI boundary before optional promotion

invocation.recommended: explicit user invocation only, followed by a second confirmation of the resolved roster, time, quota, and provider routes
invocation.notAuthorized: automatic paid dispatch, implementation, install, login, publish, commit, or deployment

execution.recommended: in-session scout, then bounded external read-only proposers/refiners and recorded aggregation only after confirmation
execution.alternatives: single-model in-session planning; CLI-only promotion without the Flask control room
execution.webui: exclude from promotion pending a real access-control and network-origin boundary

changes.summary: Add the full-tree disposition, six-pass evidence, provider and Web UI promotion boundaries, open policy questions, validation, and limitations without changing any baseline source, asset, or license bytes.

questions.question: Should a high-stakes task implicitly activate a multi-provider run?
questions.recommendation: No; require explicit invocation and retain the second pre-dispatch roster/time/quota confirmation.
questions.rationale: The workflow consumes shared provider quota and can run for 12-25 minutes or longer.

questions.question: Should the cited paper support measured-sounding claims about this repo-planning implementation?
questions.recommendation: No; preserve the citation as provenance and label extrapolated quality or wall-clock claims as unmeasured hypotheses.
questions.rationale: The paper evaluates a different chat-answer setting and this review ran no comparative live evaluation.

questions.question: Should the Flask control room ship in the same optional skill candidate?
questions.recommendation: Not yet; split or disable it until localhost enforcement, real non-loopback access control, origin defenses, narrower workspace roots, and explicit dispatch authorization exist.
questions.rationale: A self-issued profile isolates browser data but does not authenticate a machine user, while jobs inherit provider credentials and may inspect the default home-directory workspace root.

validation: Tier 2 graph-assisted structural review with direct source fallback for every reported coverage gap.
All four JSON schemas parsed; all Python production files passed syntax compilation with generated bytecode removed afterward.
All 47 binary assets decoded, dimension-checked, SHA-256 matched to the frozen baseline, and were visually inspected without modification.

Candidate offline suite passed 139/139 tests; repository inventory, review-contract, and local-candidate fixture suites passed 13/13, 34/34, and 2/2 tests with no provider authentication or live dispatch.

Static walkthroughs covered explicit invocation, partial provider failure, schema rejection, timeout teardown, workspace mutation, stale artifacts, attachment containment, browser profile isolation, remote-bind exposure, and paid dispatch authority.
limitations: No candidate workflow, provider call, web research, installer, network service, or live browser/provider evaluation was executed.
Model names, CLI flags, permission enforcement, authentication probes, and provider availability are time-sensitive and require current upstream verification before promotion.
No license was discovered in bounded ancestry; redistribution permission and upstream/version provenance are unknown.
Git-visible mutation detection is after-the-fact and cannot prevent, undo, or observe every external side effect.
The same reviewer authored and verified the artifacts; no independent second-model review is claimed.
